sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Bad Rothenfelde is a small spa town in Lower Saxony, and its parking policy is at the planning stage. On 7 February 2025 the municipality announced a traffic concept for the town centre, aiming at better stay quality, easier access and less motorised traffic [0]. The consultant report behind it, the Verkehrskonzept Ortskern of 17 December 2024, counted about 2,000 spaces in 39 car parks. Of the public spaces, 14 percent (274) are free and unrestricted, 39 percent (778) are reserved for customers or patients, 6 percent (124) use a parking disc and 41 percent (819) are pay-and-display or barrier-controlled [1]. The report proposes examining a shared-space-style Begegnungszone for Salinenstraße, like the existing one in Frankfurter Straße. It also looked at temporary closures of Salinenstraße and Hannoversche Straße but advised against them, because the fire brigade said they would make normal response times impossible [7]. These are recommendations; we found no council decision adopting them.

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The concept judges the present signage poor, since it is entirely static and points mainly to the Zentralparkplatz and the Heristo-Sportpark. It recommends dynamic guidance with occupancy sensors as a high-priority measure, with the design still to be worked out [4]. It also suggests graded pricing, with peripheral car parks such as Palsterkamp staying free or cheap, a bus link for outer car parks and app-based payment [5]. It describes the Zentralparkplatz as the most important car park in the centre but badly in need of renewal, and recommends a fundamental renovation at least as a long-term goal [6]. According to the municipality, quoted in the concept, the town had 12 public or semi-public charging stations, without a date, and intends to expand them step by step [8]. Arrivals by rail reach Dissen-Bad Rothenfelde station, in Dissen, and a free VOS shuttle bus (lines 475 or 467) runs from there to the central bus station [14].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Several central car parks are partly run by the Osnabrücker Parkraumgesellschaft (OPG) and partly by private owners; the tourism office says the municipal administration does not know their individual fees. Palsterkamp is free, and Zentralparkplatz/Ulmenallee is the coach parking area [9]. The OPG page for Parkplatz carpesol lists 2.00 euros for the first and second hour, 1.00 euro for each further hour and a daily maximum of 8.00 euros, with a 1.00 euro discount for visitors of the carpesol and the Freibad [10]. The Therme's FAQ describes a QR code from reception, but it carries two differing blocks, so some details may be outdated [11]. The 60-space motorhome area at the campotel charges a pure parking fee, not covered by the guest card [13].

The concept's counts, taken on Thursday 1 June and Sunday 4 June 2023, show peak occupancy of about 34 percent on the Thursday and 53 percent on the Sunday, higher because of the Therme and events. The roadside parking at the Kurpark was insufficient on the Thursday, and Kirchstraße and Am Kurpark were at times full on the Sunday. Overall it found no deficient supply but an uneven use [2]. The clinic multi-storey car park is used mostly by permit holders, with many spaces free at weekends [3]. Our own data cover only the carpesol car park (310 spaces), measured for about 60 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 30% on weekdays and 32% at weekends, weighted by spaces, and a single reading, late on a Wednesday evening, showed it full. The other car parks are not in our data.
